be mad verb

out of one’s mind

also be crazy, rave, be out of your mind, are you mad?, lose your mind

classical

Plaut. Amph. 753: num tū quoque etiam īnsānīs
Cic. Att. 7.10: nisi ego īnsāniō (Lewis & Short)

īnsāniō, īnsānīre, īnsānīvī (īnsāniī), īnsānītum

conjugation

be out of one’s mind, be mad; act like a madman

From īnsānus. Īnsānīre ex amōre, to be mad with love.

Examples

  • Hic homō ex amōre īnsānit.

    The man is mad with love.Plaut. Merc. 325

  • Quaesō edepol, num tū quoque etiam īnsānīs, quom id mē interrogās?

    Good heavens, are you mad as well, to ask me that?Plaut. Amph. 753

See also crazy, madness.

SourcesLewis & Short: insanio

Plautus, Amphitruo 753; Mercator 325.
